prompt: a photo of a door in an interior wall, with a door leaf, frame and handle
notes: Any door: interior or exterior, open or closed. Split into door_open/door_closed later by adding rows and retraining nothing -- classify_openings.py reads the class list from this file. Doors are the tall-narrow case, so zone_of() usually calls them 'vertical'.

prompt: a photo of a window in a building wall, with glass panes and a window frame
notes: Any glazed opening: window, window bay, glazed door panel, shutter-covered window. Beware: a wide window high in the frame is called 'ceiling' by zones.py::zone_of and is forced to 'other' -- see README, section 'The ceiling rule eats high windows'.

prompt: a photo of a plain wall, floor, ceiling, radiator or piece of furniture
notes: Everything that is not an opening. This one class carries a very heterogeneous set (walls, floors, ceilings, radiators, pillars, people, clutter) behind a single prompt, so it is the weakest of the three -- see README. Adding more 'other' rows is NOT supported: class names must be unique in this file.
